Here dimension means **Hausdorff dimension**. As approved by the user on
2026-10-23, assume explicitly that \(E\) is nonempty. With the convention
\(\dim_H\varnothing=0\), the printed equality would otherwise fail for
the empty set. This is a disclosed addition to the printed exercise.

Let \(n\geq0\) be an integer, let \(E\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty
compact set, and put \(I=[0,1]\). Identify \(\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\)
with \(\mathbb R^{n+1}\) and use its Euclidean metric. Prove

\[
\dim_H(E\times[0,1])=\dim_H E+1.
\]

The zero-dimensional ambient space \(\mathbb R^0\) is included. A later
formalization using a different product norm must justify the metric change.
proof:
Fix an arbitrary n∈ℕ and a nonempty compact set E⊆EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n). These are exactly the original assumptions H; compactness is retained although the selected product estimates in fact need no compactness. Let I=[0,1], let Fmax=E×I in the ordinary max product metric, and let Feuc be its coordinate image in Euclidean (n+1)-space. We prove the complete selected equality for Feuc.

Global outline and actual consumers. B004 gives finite D=dimH E. The upper-bound inference consumes B003 and B010; the positive-dimension lower-bound inference consumes B003 and B020. The zero-dimension lower-bound inference consumes E's original nonemptiness, B005 (dimension of I), B007 (isometry invariance), and B006 (monotonicity). Finally B008 transfers the result from Fmax to Feuc through the explicitly defined continuous linear equivalence YuiJoinEquiv n. B001 and B009 are used only inside B010/B020, and B002, B011 and B019 only inside B020. There is no residual class 4 assumption.

Normalization and definitions. Throughout H^a is unnormalized Hausdorff measure with diameter-power cost. B001 is the actual countable-cover formula in the selected Mathlib, including its nonempty-member supremum. For a>0, an empty cover set has ediam 0 and cost 0, and this supremum becomes simply (ediam U_i)^a. At a finite real scale δ>0, YuiContent a (ofReal δ) A is therefore exactly the problem's H^a_δ(A), with arbitrary countable covers of diameter ≤δ. The supremum over finite positive scales equals the full B001 supremum: content decreases as the permitted scale increases, so the ∞-scale term is ≤the scale-one term. No factor involving a, n, ball radii, or volume normalization has been introduced. Dimension is Mathlib's ENNReal critical exponent; B003 is precisely the problem's critical characterization. We do not use exponent zero in any covering or slicing step, so no 0^0 convention enters.

Complete reduction of B009 (positive upper bounds). Fix q>0 with H^q(A)=0 and real r,ε>0. B001 at the finite scale ofReal r implies the cover-cost infimum there is zero. Successive infimum approximation gives sets U_i covering A, ediam U_i≤ofReal r, and Σ_i(ediam U_i)^q<ofReal(ε/2). For every i the finite diameter has a real representative d_i=(ediam U_i).toReal∈[0,r]. Let b_i=ε·2^(-i-2)>0, α_i=min(r,b_i^(1/q)), and a_i=max(d_i,α_i). Then a_i>0, a_i≤r, and ediam U_i≤ofReal a_i. Since q>0, α_i^q≤b_i and a_i^q=max(d_i^q,α_i^q)≤d_i^q+b_i. The geometric sum Σ_i b_i=ε/2 gives Σ_i(ofReal a_i)^q<ofReal ε. ENNReal coercion and power identities are used only for nonnegative finite real arguments; every cost series stays ENNReal-valued. Empty and singleton U_i remain unchanged. Positive majorants a_i, rather than positive actual diameters, make this proof valid even when X is a singleton. This gives the exact B009 interface from B001 and elementary positive powers and geometric series.

Complete reduction of B010 (subdivision upper bound). Fix q>0 and H^q(A)=0. For any positive extended target scale R choose a finite real r with 0<r≤1 and ofReal r≤R. For each ε>0, B009 supplies an r-cover and bounds a_i with Σ_i(ofReal a_i)^q<ofReal ε. Let N_i=ceil(1/a_i), a positive integer. Since a_i≤1, 1/N_i≤a_i and N_i≤1/a_i+1≤2/a_i. For j∈{0,…,N_i−1} put J_ij=[j/N_i,(j+1)/N_i]. These closed intervals cover I: use the last interval at t=1 and j=floor(N_i t) when t<1. Then U_i×J_ij cover A×I, and their ediam is ≤ofReal a_i because each coordinate edistance is so bounded and the product uses maximum distance. The countable index Σ_i Fin N_i can be enumerated by ℕ; padding by empty sets adds zero (q+1)-cost. Nonnegative series can be regrouped without a summability assumption. The cost is bounded by
Σ_i N_i a_i^(q+1) ≤2Σ_i a_i^q <2ε
in ENNReal. Here a_i>0 justifies division by a_i and the power identity. Apply this with ε smaller than half any desired cost tolerance. Thus the product has covers of arbitrarily small (q+1)-cost at every positive R; B001 gives H^(q+1)(A×I)=0. The proof is independent of ambient dimension.

Complete reduction of B019 (slicing an individual cover). Fix s>0 and an extended scale 0<r<∞, and let (V_i) be any r-cover of A×I. Set ρ_i=ediam V_i, A_i=fst''V_i and B_i=snd''V_i. For any two points in V_i, each coordinate edistance is bounded by their max product edistance, hence by ρ_i. Taking diameter suprema gives ediam A_i≤ρ_i and ediam B_i≤ρ_i. All ρ_i are finite because ρ_i≤r. For a nonempty V_i, B_i is a nonempty bounded subset of ℝ. Order completeness gives B_i⊆[sInf B_i,sSup B_i]; put J_i equal to that closed interval. B011 gives volume(J_i)=ofReal(sSup B_i−sInf B_i)=ediam B_i≤ρ_i. If V_i=∅ use J_i=∅, which satisfies the same containment and bound. In either case J_i is measurable. This argument does not assert measurability of V_i, A_i or B_i.

Let c=YuiContent s r A, possibly ∞. For each t∈I define W_i(t)=A_i if t∈J_i and ∅ otherwise. For x∈A, some i satisfies (x,t)∈V_i, hence x∈A_i and t∈B_i⊆J_i. Thus W_i(t) cover A and have ediam≤r. By the defining infimum of content and monotonicity of positive powers,
c≤Σ_i ρ_i^s 1_{J_i}(t), t∈I.
At an unselected or empty member the corresponding diameter-power cost is zero because s>0. Integrate this inequality against ν=volume.restrict I. B011 gives ν(univ)=volume(I)=1, and the integral of the constant c is c, including c=∞. Each summand is measurable because J_i is closed (or empty). B002 interchanges the nonnegative integral and series, and the integral of a constant times an indicator is that constant times ν(J_i). Consequently
c≤Σ_i ρ_i^s ν(J_i)≤Σ_iρ_i^sρ_i=Σ_iρ_i^(s+1).
The final power identity holds for finite ρ_i>0 by the usual addition law, and at ρ_i=0 because s>0. No signed integral, integrability assumption, finite-content assumption, ε-limit, or subtraction of infinite values is used. This is B019. It is the supplied slicing argument with the measurable closed hull in place of the open enlargement.

Complete reduction of B020 (measure comparison). For each finite positive scale r, B019 holds for every r-cover V of A×I, so take the infimum over V to get YuiContent s r A≤YuiContent(s+1) r (A×I). By B001 and positivity of s and s+1, the supremum of these contents over finite positive r is exactly H^s(A), respectively H^(s+1)(A×I). Taking suprema proves H^s(A)≤H^(s+1)(A×I). In particular H^s(A)=∞ forces H^(s+1)(A×I)=∞.

Ambient finiteness. Apply B004 to the actual Euclidean E: dimH E<∞. The codomain of dimension is [0,∞], so it is automatically nonnegative. Define the ordinary real D=(dimH E).toReal; non-top finiteness gives dimH E=ofReal D and D≥0. The source of B004 bounds dimH E by the real finrank n using monotonicity into the ambient whole space; this remains valid at n=0. Thus all following approaches q↓D and s↑D use finite real exponents.

Upper bound. For every real q>D, q>0. Regard q as a nonnegative real exponent. B003 gives H^q(E)=0. B010, applied with X=EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) and its standard Borel structure, yields H^(q+1)(Fmax)=0. Since zero is not ∞, B003 implies dimH Fmax≤ofReal(q+1). Therefore dimH Fmax≤ofReal(D+1)=dimH E+1: if the inequality failed, density would give a real q>D with ofReal(q+1)<dimH Fmax, contradicting the preceding bound. One can first take q=D+1 to see dimH Fmax is finite and then use ordinary real density. This argument works unchanged at n=0.

Lower bound for positive D. Assume D>0. For every 0<s<D, B003 gives H^s(E)=∞. B020 yields H^(s+1)(Fmax)=∞, and B003 gives ofReal(s+1)≤dimH Fmax. As s ranges increasingly to the finite positive D, real order density gives ofReal(D+1)≤dimH Fmax. More explicitly, any proposed strict smaller right side would admit 0<s<D with dimH Fmax<ofReal(s+1), a contradiction.

Lower bound for D=0. The original nonemptiness hypothesis supplies x₀∈E. The map f:ℝ→EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)×ℝ, f(t)=(x₀,t), is an isometry: max(dist(x₀,x₀),dist(t,u))=dist(t,u). B007 and B005 give dimH(f''I)=dimH I=1. Since f''I⊆Fmax, B006 gives 1≤dimH Fmax. For D=0 this is dimH E+1≤dimH Fmax. It also covers n=0, for which the ambient space is a singleton and the ambient dimension bound forces D=0. No positive ambient-cardinality assumption is used.

Euclidean metric transfer. YuiJoinEquiv n is explicitly the composition of (i) PiLp.continuousLinearEquiv 2 ℝ on the Euclidean base, product the identity on ℝ; (ii) swapping the two factors; (iii) Fin.consEquivL, adjoining the real coordinate to a finite vector; and (iv) the inverse PiLp coordinate equivalence in dimension n+1. All are existing continuous real linear equivalences, including when n=0. Its coordinate formula is (x,t)↦WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons t (WithLp.ofLp x)). Thus its image of Fmax is exactly the original product set realized in Euclidean (n+1)-space, with the interval coordinate first. If the product is written with the interval coordinate last, a coordinate permutation carries one realization to the other; it is an isometry because it preserves the sum of squared coordinate differences. B007 preserves dimension for that optional reordering. B008 gives
dimH Feuc=dimH Fmax.
This explicitly justifies the change from max product metric to the requested Euclidean metric; it does not equate those metrics or their Hausdorff measures. The upper and lower bounds now yield dimH Feuc=dimH E+1, the full selected target with exactly the original assumptions.

Classification and provenance. B001, B006 and B007 name exact whole-type Mathlib statements; the other class 1 items are explicitly adapted specializations/conjunctions of the cited source statements. B009, B010, B019 and B020 are the concrete recursive class 3 derivations just given. No public Lean-library or textbook theorem is assumed. Failed external metadata access in the investigation is not theorem evidence and is not used. The selected environment's native inspection binds the actual source revision; no unseen commit is asserted. The complete planning route was selected with every new Lean proof body null; proof bodies are added only after selection and must pass the complete assembly check. Selection and compilation are implementation checks; separate basis review and Audit A still decide statement fidelity and application correctness.
Auxiliary-universe repair after actual assembly feedback. The four prepared cover/slicing lemmas B009, B010, B019 and B020 are specialized to ambient metric types in Lean Type (universe 0). Every EuclideanSpace, its product, countable cover index and real interval in the original problem lies there. This is a weaker auxiliary statement sufficient at every consumer, not a change to n, E, H or P. B001 remains the full universe-polymorphic native source theorem. Local helpers use that native theorem at universe 0. No Kuratowski embedding, separability theorem or universe-changing representation is needed in this repaired route.
For the two final product-measure interfaces B010 and B020, the repaired Lean statements additionally require SecondCountableTopology X. This is available on every finite-dimensional Euclidean consumer, including n=0, and ensures that the ordinary measurable product has its Borel structure when B001 is applied. The cover extraction B009 and the individual-cover bound B019 need no such topological assumption. This is a sufficient specialization of the independent frontier proposals; the derivations above apply unchanged and use no separability or embedding theorem.

import Mathlib
open Set MeasureTheory
open scoped ENNReal NNReal
noncomputable section

abbrev YuiRn (n : ℕ) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)

def YuiContent {X : Type*} [EMetricSpace X] (a : ℝ) (r : ℝ≥0∞) (A : Set X) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ⨅ (U : ℕ → Set X) (_ : A ⊆ ⋃ i, U i) (_ : ∀ i, Metric.ediam (U i) ≤ r),
    ∑' i, (Metric.ediam (U i)) ^ a

def YuiJoinEquiv (n : ℕ) : (YuiRn n × ℝ) ≃L[ℝ] YuiRn (n + 1) :=
  (((PiLp.continuousLinearEquiv 2 ℝ (fun _ : Fin n => ℝ)).prodCongr
      (ContinuousLinearEquiv.refl ℝ ℝ)).trans
    (ContinuousLinearEquiv.prodComm ℝ (Fin n → ℝ) ℝ)).trans
    ((Fin.consEquivL ℝ (fun _ : Fin (n + 1) => ℝ)).trans
      (PiLp.continuousLinearEquiv 2 ℝ (fun _ : Fin (n + 1) => ℝ)).symm)

dependencies.statement: For every Borel extended metric space X, real a and arbitrary A⊆X, unnormalized Hausdorff measure is the supremum over positive extended scales r of the infimum of countable r-cover costs; the cost is Σ_i sup_{h:U_i nonempty}(ediam U_i)^a.

dependencies.justification: At a finite positive scale r, take the infimum of B019 over all r-covers V of the product to obtain YuiContent s r A≤YuiContent(s+1) r (A×I). Since s and s+1 are positive, empty-member costs in B001 reduce to plain diameter powers, so these contents match its infima. Take suprema over finite positive r. This is the whole B001 supremum: the r=∞ term is at most the r=1 term by monotonicity of admissible cover infima. Thus H^s(A)≤H^(s+1)(A×I). No finite-content premise or compactness is used. Assembly repair: restrict auxiliary ambient types to Type, which contains all target spaces. This removes independent generated universe levels; no original parameter, domain or assumption changes. Assume SecondCountableTopology X in this auxiliary theorem so that the ordinary measurable product has its Borel structure. EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) has this instance for all n, including zero.

propositions.statement: Let n be an arbitrary natural number, E⊆Euclidean n-space be nonempty and compact, I=[0,1], Fmax=E×I with the max product metric, and Feuc the coordinate realization of E×I with the Euclidean metric in dimension n+1. These are the original target hypotheses, including n=0.
For every n∈ℕ and nonempty compact E⊆Euclidean n-space, its Hausdorff dimension is a finite nonnegative value D, so dimH E=ofReal D in [0,∞].
For every n∈ℕ and nonempty compact E⊆Euclidean n-space, dimH(E×[0,1])≤dimH E+1 when the product has the max metric.
For every n∈ℕ and nonempty compact E⊆Euclidean n-space with dimH E>0, dimH E+1≤dimH(E×[0,1]) in the max product metric.
For every n∈ℕ and nonempty compact E⊆Euclidean n-space with dimH E=0, dimH E+1≤dimH(E×[0,1]) in the max product metric.
For every n∈ℕ and nonempty compact E⊆Euclidean n-space, dimH(E×[0,1])=dimH E+1 in the max product metric.

For every n∈ℕ and E⊆Euclidean n-space, the Euclidean coordinate image of E×[0,1] under YuiJoinEquiv n has the same Hausdorff dimension as E×[0,1] with the max metric. The image uses interval coordinate first; moving it last is an isometric coordinate permutation. This holds at n=0.

Here dimension means **Hausdorff dimension**. As approved by the user on
2026-10-23, assume explicitly that \(E\) is nonempty. With the convention
\(\dim_H\varnothing=0\), the printed equality would otherwise fail for
the empty set. This is a disclosed addition to the printed exercise.

Let \(n\geq0\) be an integer, let \(E\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty
compact set, and put \(I=[0,1]\). Identify \(\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\)
with \(\mathbb R^{n+1}\) and use its Euclidean metric. Prove

\[
\dim_H(E\times[0,1])=\dim_H E+1.
\]

The zero-dimensional ambient space \(\mathbb R^0\) is included. A later
formalization using a different product norm must justify the metric change.
